t.6.2.1: To that Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who was worn down by grief, the illustrious Sugrīva spoke words that would dispel his sorrow.
t.6.2.2: Why do you torment yourself with grief, O hero, like some ordinary man? Do not be so; cast off your grief, as an ungrateful man casts off friendship.
t.6.2.3: For I see no ground for your grief, O Rāghava, now that news has been obtained and the dwelling place of the enemy is known.
t.6.2.4: You are steadfast, versed in the scriptures, wise and learned, O Rāghava. Cast off this sinful thought that ruins your purpose, acting as one who is master of himself.
t.6.2.6: For one who is without energy, dejected, and whose mind is overwhelmed by grief, all his aims come to ruin, and he falls into calamity.
t.6.2.7: All these leaders of our monkey troops are heroic and capable, and for the sake of what is dear to you they are resolved to enter even fire.
t.6.2.5: Having crossed the ocean teeming with great crocodiles, we shall scale Laṅkā and slay your enemy.
t.6.2.8: From the joy of these monkeys I know it, and my conviction on this point is firm: by valor I shall bring back Sītā, having slain the enemy as is fitting.
t.6.2.9: O Rāghava, act in such a way that a bridge may be built here, so that we may behold that city of the king of the rākṣasas.
t.6.2.10: For once you have seen that city of Laṅkā, standing on the summit of Trikūṭa, regard Rāvaṇa as already slain in battle from that very sight.
t.6.2.11: Once a bridge has been built across the ocean as far as the vicinity of Laṅkā, and the whole army has crossed over, let it be regarded as won.
t.6.2.12: For these monkeys, who can take any form at will, are heroes in battle. Therefore, O king, enough of this despondent state of mind, which ruins every purpose.
t.6.2.14: For to brave, great-souled men such as you, grief, whether over what is destroyed or over what is lost, is the ruin of every aim.
t.6.2.13: For in this world grief saps a man's valor. But do what must be done by a man who relies on heroism: at this time, O greatly wise one, take your stand on courage with vigor.
t.6.2.15: But you, the foremost of the wise, well versed in the meaning of all the śāstras, ought here to conquer the enemy together with counsellors such as I.
t.6.2.16: For I see no one in the three worlds, O Rāghava, who could stand facing you in battle when you have taken up your bow.
t.6.2.17: Your task, entrusted to the monkeys, will not fail. Before long, having crossed the imperishable ocean, you will see Sītā.
t.6.2.18: Therefore, enough of clinging to grief; take hold of anger, O lord of the earth. Kṣatriyas who remain inactive are feeble, but everyone fears one who is fierce.
t.6.2.19: Having come here together with us, reflect with your subtle intellect on a means of crossing the terrible ocean, the lord of rivers.
t.6.2.20: For these monkeys, heroes in battle and able to take any form at will, will crush those enemies with showers of rocks and trees.
t.6.2.21: Somehow we shall see our way across the ocean, the abode of Varuṇa. Why say more, and in so many ways? In every respect you will be victorious.
